blurb: The SQL of a `D1`, `Postgres` or `MySql` call must be a string literal, or a `String` constant bound to one, so it is fixed when the program compiles and no request data can become part of the statement: that is how SQL injection happens. An interpolated string, a parameter or a `let` binding is refused. Put the value in the parameter list, as `?1` with `Text(id)`, which is always bound and never spliced in.
example:
let _ <- Orders.all("SELECT id FROM orders WHERE id = '\(id)'", [])         // ✗ built at run time

let _ <- Orders.all("SELECT id FROM orders WHERE id = ?1", [Text(id)])      // ✓ bound
summary: A `D1` or `Postgres` statement's SQL (the first argument of `all`, `first`, `run`, `select` or `firstAs`, or the `sql` of a `SqlStatement` or a `PgStatement`) is neither a string literal nor a bare reference to a `String` constant bound to one, so data could be spliced into it instead of bound as a `SqlValue` or `PgValue` parameter (standard-library P4c, Hyperdrive H1 and H3).
